population: 70 preregistered nationally representative U.S. survey experiments
intervention: text-based survey interventions; up to 12 arms and first 3 outcomes
outcome_wording_scale: effects harmonized to percentage points of scale range
effect_estimate: predicted versus observed r=0.85; calibration slope human-on-LLM=0.56; RMSE=11.09 pp
uncertainty: r 95% CI [0.81,0.88]; adjusted r=0.92 [0.89,0.94]; adjusted RMSE=10.59 pp
moderator_results: subgroup predictive r reported as 0.90 White, 0.86 Black, 0.90 male, 0.90 female, 0.87 Republican, 0.85 Democrat; original interactions were uncommon
relevance: validates individual simulation for U.S. text survey ATE rank prediction and warns magnitude inflation
limitations: different topics/outcomes; GPT-4 implementation; reference arm varied; forecasts systematically too large

population: 30 U.S. survey experiments unpublished by GPT-4 cutoff
effect_estimate: r=0.90; calibration slope=0.60; adjusted RMSE=10.22 pp
relevance: supports more credible out-of-training validation
limitations: proprietary training data cannot be audited completely

effect_estimate: overall r=0.39 and calibration slope=0.34; survey megastudies r=0.43; text treatments r=0.45
relevance: closest high-level expectation for benchmark pooled rank performance
limitations: RMSE not comparable across original scales; includes field/nontext studies

population: 62-country climate megastudy plus replications in 12 and 27 countries
intervention: three LLMs simulate realized climate interventions
effect_estimate: LLM response MAE 24.3-26.1 pp but ATE absolute error 8.7-9.4 pp; supervised baselines ATE error 4.3-4.4 pp
moderator_results: realism-ATE accuracy rank relation near zero; divergence larger for behavior
relevance: prohibits selecting a Tier 1 method on marginal realism alone
limitations: cross-national; tested smaller/older models; not this benchmark

population: human benchmark datasets and silicon configurations
outcome_wording_scale: participant ranks, distributions, and cross-scale relations
effect_estimate: configuration-dependent participant-rank rho ranged -0.24 to 0.40 and -0.29 to 0.22; cross-scale r estimates ranged -0.40 to 0.78 against human r=0.26
relevance: requires prompt and aggregation choices to be frozen externally
limitations: constructs are not climate-treatment effects; specification results do not name a universally best configuration

effect_estimate: 48% of regression coefficients differed significantly from ANES counterparts; among those differences, 32% reversed sign
moderator_results: synthetic variance compressed; outputs sensitive to minor prompts and a three-month model update
relevance: strong warning against trusting Tier 1 subgroup realism or adding post-hoc noise
limitations: not causal-treatment validation; GPT-3.5-era models

citation: Rode et al. (2021), Journal of Environmental Psychology
control: no information, unrelated task, or other controls
outcome_wording_scale: belief, concern, worry, and policy attitudes; standardized
effect_estimate: Hedges g=0.08; consensus-only g=0.09
uncertainty: overall 95% CI [0.05,0.10], 95% prediction interval [-0.04,0.19]; consensus CI [0.05,0.13]
moderator_results: intervention type and political affiliation were not significant moderators; policy effects smaller than belief; 10 percentage-point higher female share associated with g +0.03
relevance: empirical small-effect prior; permits null/negative cells and proximal-distal ordering
limitations: 396 dependent effects from 76 experiments; wording/scales/control types vary

effect_estimate: largest belief gain 2.3% for decreasing psychological distance
moderator_results: effects largely limited to non-skeptics and varied by prebelief and country
relevance: prior for benchmark belief and concern outcomes
limitations: global, not only U.S.; intervention wording differs; percentage is reported study metric

effect_estimate: largest policy gain 2.6%
moderator_results: effects varied by initial climate belief and country
relevance: prior for general/specific policy support
limitations: global transportability; no filler control

effect_estimate: largest sharing gain 12.1%
moderator_results: heterogeneous by initial belief
relevance: upper-bound analogue for low-cost behavioral intention
limitations: not a donation/signup; self-report intention

outcome_wording_scale: effortful tree-planting task, up to 8 pages
effect_estimate: no intervention increased tree planting; several reduced it
moderator_results: effects differed by initial belief
relevance: strong null/negative prior for behavioral endpoints
limitations: task-specific behavior and global sample

citation: Geiger et al. (2024), Nature Human Behaviour
outcome_wording_scale: perceived consensus 0-100; climate reality/human-cause belief; worry; public-action support
effect_estimate: d=0.47 consensus perception; d=0.06 reality belief; d=0.10 human-cause belief; d=0.05 worry; d=0.02 public action
moderator_results: larger updating with low familiarity/misperception; right-leaning and low-trust groups did not backfire and often updated more
relevance: direct prior for Consensus condition; proximal effects dominate distal policy
limitations: convenience and highly educated sample; estimate-and-reveal design; not exact benchmark wording

outcome_wording_scale: human-caused climate belief and scientist skill/bias, each 0-100 across consensus levels
effect_estimate: history increased climate belief 2.36 points and proconsensus-scientist skill 2.08 points
relevance: direct prior for institutional history, modeling/methods, and scientist-credibility messages
limitations: outcomes repeatedly evaluated at hypothetical consensus levels; no behavioral endpoints

intervention: institutional constraints on bias in climate science
effect_estimate: proconsensus-scientist skill +1.94 points
relevance: prior for peer review, funding, institutions, and methods conditions
limitations: no filler control; little effect on perceived bias

citation: Thomas-Walters et al. (2026), Global Environmental Psychology
population: quota samples in U.S., U.K., and India
intervention: short flood/heat attribution messages with 3x or 200% framing
control: cheetah filler pure control and extreme-weather active control
outcome_wording_scale: belief weather made more likely/worse, standardized; worry; government action; link click
effect_estimate: main d=0.06 to 0.14; 4.5-6.1 pp top-category increase; U.S. best flood-percent d=0.18
uncertainty: main active-control [0.03,0.10]; best treatments [0.10,0.18]; U.S. flood-percent [0.12,0.24]
moderator_results: no event-type or number-frame difference; U.S. and U.K. effects larger than India
relevance: direct prior for state-tailored Extreme weather predictions
limitations: target uses different states/weather and trust outcomes; adjusted for premeasure

citation: Thomas-Walters et al. (2026), Global Environmental Psychology
population: quota samples in U.S., U.K., and India
effect_estimate: worry largest d=0.06; government action d=0.03 for two heat messages and null in U.S./India; link click 3.2% overall
relevance: shrinks transport from attribution belief to benchmark concern/policy/behavior
limitations: cross-country pooled secondary outcomes; link not newsletter

citation: Voelkel et al. (2026), Nature Climate Change
population: U.S. national nonprobability sample matched on key demographics
outcome_wording_scale: belief, concern, general/specific policy, political/nonpolitical intentions, donation, all 0-100
effect_estimate: six messages changed multiple attitudes by 1-4 pp; no message increased donation
moderator_results: persuasiveness varied little across party lines; targeted-message heterogeneity largely unsupported
relevance: closest external design: U.S., same filler mixture, short messages, multiple benchmark-like outcomes
limitations: pre/post measures and some covariate-adjusted primary analyses; model cutoff leakage risk for retrospective LLM validation

outcome_wording_scale: binary newsletter, donation and other advocacy actions
effect_estimate: control: newsletter 22%, donation 49%, representative letter 41%, petition 19%, video share 16%
relevance: baseline anchors for signup and donation; demonstrates wording-specific levels
limitations: advocacy newsletters and donation choices differ materially from benchmark offer/AMS allocation

effect_estimate: public advocacy +0.10; political advocacy +0.06
relevance: upper-end evidence for strong efficacy/emotion combinations; not a generic text prior
limitations: composites mix binary and intention measures; winner selected among many conditions

control: informed control describing policy goals, benefits and $20 monthly cost
effect_estimate: best 3-module ensemble +20.10 policy points and +$1.31 donation; single efficacy +13.86 and +$0.61
moderator_results: weighted results similar; no detected order effects
relevance: post-model-cutoff evaluation and evidence that coherent ensembles can outperform components
limitations: multi-module dosage and informed costly-policy control unlike benchmark; source study is a preprint

population: randomized field trials; mostly U.S./Canada and Europe
effect_estimate: d=-0.093 in coding where negative is improvement; probability of benefit 6.6%
moderator_results: small-study/self-selection patterns; no durable effect
relevance: strong caution against translating attitudes into actual behavior
limitations: longer field interventions and behavior definitions differ from a one-shot survey intention

citation: Amazeen et al. (2025), npj Climate Action
intervention: Exxon native advertisement; disclosure; UN-source inoculation
control: restaurant-review social post and ad without inoculation
effect_estimate: misleading investment claim means 4.43 no inoculation, 4.21 inoculation, 3.87 control; inoculation versus no inoculation p=0.043
moderator_results: inoculation reduced but sometimes did not eliminate misleading belief; no reduction in true climate belief
relevance: direct evidence for oil-industry misinformation/inoculation condition
limitations: focuses brand/claim belief rather than trust composite; condition Ns and larger parent analysis differ

citation: Hausfather et al. (2020), Geophysical Research Letters
effect_estimate: 10 of 17 projections consistent with observations on raw temperature; 14 of 17 consistent after accounting for forcing mismatches
relevance: factual basis for Model accuracy condition
limitations: this is evidence content, not a randomized communication effect

citation: Goldberg et al. (2021), Nature Climate Change
outcome_wording_scale: existence, causes, harms, risk, issue importance
effect_estimate: campaign increased climate understanding by several percentage points
moderator_results: effects targeted Republicans in two competitive districts
relevance: evidence for Former skeptics and conservative messenger interviews
limitations: video campaign/repeated exposure, localized field setting, not a one-shot national text

citation: Andre et al. (2024/2026), Review of Economics and Statistics
intervention: correct actual climate-friendly behavior or norm prevalence
outcome_wording_scale: donation/willingness index; policy support; political action
effect_estimate: behavior-information treatment policy support +0.09 SD; norm-information +0.07 SD
moderator_results: effects strongest among climate skeptics; prior underestimation conditions response
relevance: evidence for high-public-trust/social-norm-type information and possible skeptical subgroup effects
limitations: different norm content and outcomes; first wave informed treatment values

intervention: categorical versus instrumental scientist value judgments crossed with policy congruence
effect_estimate: no transportable ATE extracted; policy congruence influenced evaluations
moderator_results: respondent-policy congruence is central
relevance: qualitative prior for Social justice and policy-role/trust effects
limitations: within-subject design and no directly portable numerical effect

citation: Leiserowitz et al. (2026), Climate Change in the American Mind
outcome_wording_scale: happening, human cause, worry and engagement categorical items
effect_estimate: 68% happening; 59% mostly human-caused; 66% at least somewhat worried; 29% very worried; 65% personally important
moderator_results: large known partisan/ideological gradients in the series
relevance: current baseline anchor only, with wording/scale crosswalk required
limitations: not experimental and questions are not identical to benchmark sliders

effect_estimate: 34% say climate policies usually help the economy and 34% say hurt
moderator_results: Republicans: 56% hurt; Democrats: 52% help
relevance: baseline/heterogeneity anchor for policy outcomes
limitations: not same item wording or 0-100 scale

citation: Annenberg Science and Public Health Knowledge Monitor (2024)
effect_estimate: 65% expressed trust in climate scientists
relevance: baseline anchor for climate-scientist trust
limitations: not identical multidimensional or 0-100 wording

citation: National Science Board, Science & Engineering Indicators 2024
effect_estimate: public trust in science remains high; cites 54% wanting climate scientists to have a larger policy role and 18% saying they understand solutions very well
moderator_results: knowledge/familiarity positively associated with trust
relevance: baseline for policy-role and general institutional trust only
limitations: aggregates source surveys; item wording differs
